title: Error boundaries & fault tolerance
lead1: A crashing subtree does not mean a blank page.
lead2: can fence rendering errors locally, swap in a fallback UI, and offer a retry; but errors in events, timers, and Promises are invisible to it by nature — those must be
lead3: thrown back into the render phase. The four cases below are all clickable right now.
case1Title: ① Render-phase error: boundaries catch this natively
case1Hint: A component throws inside render; the nearest ErrorBoundary catches it and renders the fallback instead.
case1Crashed: The subtree has crashed; the rest of the page is unaffected
case2Title: ② Event & async errors: use useAsyncError to throw back into render
case2Hint1: Click any button below; the error will be
case2Hint2: thrown on the next render, so the boundary catches it too — the three entry points (event / timer / Promise) behave identically.
case3Title: ③ Control group: a direct throw is invisible to boundaries
case3Hint1: This button is also inside an ErrorBoundary, but it throws directly in the event callback. Click it: the console logs an error, but
case3Hint2: fallback UI appears — because event handling happens outside React rendering.
case3Fallback: You will not see this line — boundaries cannot catch errors in events
case3Reason: This is exactly why case ② exists.
case4Title: ④ resetKeys: auto-reset when dependencies change
case4Hint1: A common scenario: after switching user / data source, the old error state should clear automatically, rather than making the user click retry. Pass the dependency into
case4AutoReset: Change the resetKey on the right and the boundary auto-resets
logHint2: usually hooks into log reporting. Here we keep only the last 5 entries.
logEmpty: No errors captured yet — click a few buttons above

parts.renderErrorSuffix: : this error was thrown during render
parts.eventErr: An error thrown in the event callback — caught by the boundary
parts.timerErr: An error thrown in a timer — caught by the boundary
parts.promiseErr: An error thrown in a Promise — caught by the boundary
parts.naiveErr: Direct throw: boundaries cannot see it (the console logs the error, but the page does not degrade)
